answer: A durable defense is a work-history ledger: each agent earns reputation only by completing verifiable tasks over time, recorded in a shared atlas of past performance. A newcomer cannot simply spawn a plume of fake identities, because each new identity starts with zero history and must pay the same slow cost in compute, fees, and time as everyone else. Like seasoning timber, trust takes time to harden, so flooding the network with cheap copies buys no influence until each copy has done real, checkable work.
